places.name: Persepolis
places.summary: Ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Empire; inscribed by UNESCO in 1979.

facts.t: Inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1979.
Site of the October 1971 celebrations of 2,500 years of the Iranian monarchy.

places.name: Golestan Palace
places.summary: Qajar-era royal complex in the historic core of Tehran.

facts.t: Originally built in the Safavid period; took its most characteristic form in the 19th century as the Qajar family's royal residence and seat of power.
Inscribed on the World Heritage List on 23 June 2013.

places.name: Trans-Iranian Railway
places.summary: 1,394 km standard-gauge line opened fully in 1938.

facts.t: Connects the Caspian Sea in the north to the Persian Gulf in the south; opened fully in 1938.
Inscribed on the World Heritage List on 25 July 2021.
Built during Reza Shah's reign as part of the expansion of roads, railways and state factories.

places.name: University of Tehran
places.summary: Iran's first European-style university, founded in the mid-1930s.

facts.t: LoC: established in 1935 as the country's first European-style university. Another source says inaugurated 1934.

places.name: Azadi (Shahyad) Tower
places.summary: Marble-clad monument completed in 1971, designed by Hossein Amanat.

facts.t: Completed in 1971; designed by Hossein Amanat; originally named Shahyad Tower.

places.name: Tehran Museum of Contemporary Art
places.summary: Museum inaugurated in 1977 and designed by Kamran Diba.

facts.t: Inaugurated in 1977; designed by Kamran Diba with Nader Ardalan.
